title: Spending per pupil beside results, eleven districts
question: Do the districts that spend more per pupil get better results, and where does San Francisco sit?
finding: In 2023-24 San Francisco was number 3 of 11 for day-to-day spending per pupil ($25,249) and number 2 for English results (53.7% meeting the standard). Across the eleven districts the higher spenders tended to have the lower English results (rank correlation -0.51): the highest spender, Oakland Unified, had 33.1% meeting the standard and the lowest, Elk Grove Unified, 51.7%. That is the pattern the State's funding formula produces by itself, because it sends more money to districts with more high-need pupils.
how: Day-to-day spending per pupil from the federal survey for fiscal 2024, beside the State's district results for school year 2023-24. The rank correlation is Spearman's, over eleven districts; with so few it is a description, not a test.
limits: Eleven districts cannot show what money buys. Spending and results are linked by many things besides management, above all who the pupils are: the State formula, as the district's own budget release describes it, gives more to districts serving more high-need pupils, and those districts also start from lower scores, which by itself produces a pattern of "more money, lower results". A district where living costs are high must pay more to hire and keep staff, and one with many small schools, or with many pupils who are learning English, have disabilities or are poor, will spend more per pupil for honest reasons; none of those is measured here.
